footer: Everyone deserves clear information and a fair chance to get help. This site prepares your next step. Agencies decide on assistance and repairs. Follow current instructions from your water provider or health department.

name: Your name
required: Please fill in the required fields.
confirmDelete: Delete this saved item? This cannot be undone.
uploadIntro: Choose a file, paste the words, or enter a result yourself. Nothing is sent to AI without your permission.
file: Choose a PDF, photo, text file or CSV
fileHelp: Up to 10 MB. PDFs can have up to 12 pages. Clear, straight photos work best. Reading a photo may take a minute.
textHint: You can remove your name, address or account number before using AI.
readFileError: We could not read that file. Try a smaller file, a clearer photo, or paste the words below.
reviewText: Please check the words against your original document. Photo reading can make mistakes.
noResults: We could not reliably find the results. Add them yourself or ask the AI helper. Keep your original report open.
qualifier: Sign or note beside the amount
basis: For nitrate: how is it reported?
checkedResult: I checked this result, its unit and any sign against my report.
reportLimit: A result describes the sample tested. It cannot show everything in your water or predict a health problem. Keep the original report.
confirmedResults: Here is what to follow up on
confirm_result: Check this result against the original report first.
below_reporting: The report gives a testing limit or says this was not detected. That does not mean the amount is zero. Ask the lab whether the test was sensitive enough for your concern.
microbe_followup: Contact your health department promptly about this result and what water to use. A household filter may not remove germs.
microbe_guidance: Ask the lab what this germ test means and whether another sample is needed.
unit_check: We need the exact amount and unit to help compare this result. Ask the lab to explain them.
lead_followup: Lead was reported. Ask your water provider or health department how to reduce exposure and whether to test again. Boiling does not remove lead. Children and pregnant people need particular care.
arsenic_followup: This amount is above the federal public-water limit for arsenic. Ask your health department about treatment and retesting. Private wells are not covered by that federal rule.
nitrate_basis: Ask the lab whether this is reported as nitrogen or as nitrate. The same number can mean different amounts.
nitrate_followup: This amount is above the federal public-water limit for this substance. Contact your health department promptly, especially if water is used for infant formula. Boiling does not remove nitrate.
pfas_followup: This PFAS substance was reported. Ask your provider or health department about this exact substance, the amount found, and treatment options.
report_context: This result alone does not establish that the water is safe. Ask the lab how to interpret it for your sample and whether more testing is needed.
aiDescription: The AI helper can explain this document in your language. It can make mistakes. Review the answer before using it.
aiConsent: I agree to send the text shown above to Google's AI service for this explanation. I have removed details I do not want to share.
aiUnavailable: The AI helper is unavailable right now. You can still read a file, enter results, prepare letters and save your steps.
aiReview: AI draft — check it against your document.
billHint: Understand the charges and prepare a billing question.
assistanceHint: Prepare a request for testing, bill or repair help.
filtersIntro: First choose what your test found. A filter must be tested for that exact substance. Buying a filter may not be your first step if you have not tested your water.
substances: What do you need to reduce?
noResultYet: I do not have a test result
gallons: Drinking and cooking water per day (gallons)
gallonsHelp: 1 gallon is about 3.8 liters. Use your household's total. Higher use means more replacements.
noPlumbing: I need a filter that does not connect to the plumbing.
replacement: Replacement filters in the first year
noFullMatch: No listed product is confirmed for everything you selected. Ask the lab or health department before buying a partial match.
priceNote: Prices were checked on {date}. Check the seller before paying. These are selected options, not every product on the market.
stalePrice: These prices need a new check. Use the seller's current price before deciding.
excludedCosts: Estimates include the device and whole replacement packs. Tax, shipping, installation, electricity and extra water are not included. Replacements may be needed sooner.
proof: What this exact filter is tested to reduce
conditionArsenic: Arsenic needs extra checks. This product's claim is only for one form of arsenic and specific water conditions. Ask the lab and manufacturer before buying.
notMicrobes: These options are not a treatment plan for unsafe germs. Follow your health department's instructions.
billIntro: Paste your bill or read a file. Check every number. This checks the arithmetic; it does not verify your utility's rates.
billComplete: I included every charge, credit and previous balance. Credits must be entered as negative amounts.
billDifference: A difference can mean a missing item or a reading mistake. It does not prove an overcharge. Ask your provider for an itemized explanation and the rate schedule.
billEqual: The items entered add up to the amount due. That does not confirm the rate or water use is correct.
pipesHint: Look for a record for your exact home.
inspectionHint: Prepare a request to check pipes or a water problem.
repairFormHint: Start the USDA home-repair intake, if it fits your situation.
pipeIntro: Connected records: Denver Water, Pittsburgh Water and Minneapolis. New York City records remain in the address check. Other places can use the official directory or request a record.
pipeNotFound: We did not find an exact record. This does not mean your pipes are lead-free. Check the official map or ask your provider.
notConnected: We do not have a live connection for this place yet. Use the official directory below to find the right local office.
sourceUnavailable: The local source is not responding. Try its official page.
pipeCaution: Pipe records do not test your tap water. Unknown means the material has not been confirmed.
formIntro: This is the official USDA home-repair intake. It starts a review. It does not apply everywhere or guarantee funding.
ownHome: I own and live in this home.
rural: Check whether my address is eligible
formEligibility: USDA checks the rural address, household income and access to affordable credit. Grants also require age 62 or older and very low income. Renters can use the inspection and landlord-request tools.
formPrivate: Your answers are filled into the PDF on this device. Nothing is sent. Leave unknown answers blank. Sign only after reviewing the official form.
formExpired: This stored form needs an update. Open the official program page for the current form.
formReview: Review all pages, complete missing fields and contact USDA about how to submit. Your form has not been submitted.
localOffice: Find the office that accepts it

jointHint: Invite others to support one shared request.
whatHappenedHelp: Include dates, who you contacted and what they said. Use your own words.

recipientHelp: For example: your water provider, landlord or local water office.

letterRequest: What I am asking you to do

legalAid: Find free or lower-cost legal help

treatmentIntro: Record what you experienced. You do not have to disclose your race, disability, gender or immigration status. This record does not decide whether a law was broken.
whyUnfair: What makes you think the treatment was unfair?
personalOnly: Keep private details in your own record. Do not put another person's private information in a shared request.
meetingIntro: Live calendars are connected for Denver and Pittsburgh. For other places, find your local government below. Not every meeting accepts public comments.
noMeetings: No upcoming meetings were returned. Check the official calendar.
signup: How to sign up to speak
confirmDeadline: Confirm this deadline on the official page, including holiday changes.
commitment: Track a promise from an official
jointIntro: Write one clear request without private home, health or account details. Invite people you trust. They can choose to add their name. You review the list before sending it to an office.
groupTitle: Short title for the shared request
groupConsent: I understand anyone with the invitation link can read this request. I have removed private details and have permission to share what it says.
groupUnavailable: Shared invitations are unavailable right now. You can still download a request and collect permission from supporters yourself.
inviteLink: Invitation link — share only with people you choose
ownerLink: Your private organizer link — keep this to yourself

notVerifiedSignatures: These are self-entered names, not verified signatures. Nothing has been sent to an official.
joinConsent: I support this request and agree that the organizer may include my name when sending this request. Other visitors will not see my name.
joined: Your name was added. The organizer still needs to submit the request.

progressIntro: These records are private to this browser. Clearing browser data can erase them. Save a password-protected backup if you need to move them.
receivedHelp: Enter money or a bill credit you actually received. Leave blank if none. Estimates and applications are not money received.
evidence: Add a receipt, photo or letter
evidenceHelp: Stored only on this device. Up to 8 MB per file. Keep your originals.
proofStatus: Only mark a step as sent or received after it actually happens. Attach a receipt when you have one.
passwordHelp: Keep this password somewhere safe. We cannot recover it.

aiData: AI is optional. Only the text you approve is sent for an explanation. Your files are not uploaded. Shared requests are stored for 90 days; invitation links show the request, and only the organizer link shows names.
nextOfficeHelp: Start with the office that received your request. If it cannot help, ask who is responsible. For drinking-water concerns, use the regulator directory. For housing or unequal-treatment concerns, legal aid can help identify the right route and deadline.
labQuestions: Please explain the results, units, reporting limits and sample location in plain language. Which results need follow-up, and is another test needed? Please tell me about any lower-cost follow-up options.
billQuestions: Please explain the charges and give me the current rate schedule. Check whether the meter reading was actual or estimated and whether a leak adjustment, payment plan or assistance program may be available. Please confirm any shutoff date and how to request a review.
inspectionQuestions: Please provide the pipe-material record for this exact property, identify which sections are unknown, and explain how to request an inspection. Please tell me about testing, repair assistance, any cost to me, and the expected timeline.
assistanceQuestions: I need help paying for water testing, a water bill or repairs. Please tell me which current programs may fit my situation, the eligibility requirements, what documents are needed, and how I can apply with help.
repairQuestions: Please explain the problem, who is responsible for the repair, the expected start and finish dates, and any temporary help available while I wait.
followupQuestions: Please give me an update on my previous request, the person responsible, and the expected next step and date.
meetingQuestions: Please put this water concern on the record and explain what action will be taken, who is responsible and when residents will receive an update.
backupSecure: Private records need a secure page. You can use the other tools without saving.

assistanceTrackerIntro: Keep applications, deadlines and money received together. Requested money is separate from money you actually received.
rateCheckIntro: Compare a supported utility’s water-use charge with its published rate. Sewer, stormwater, taxes, old balances and other fees are checked separately.
rateScope: My bill matches the service, dates and units shown here
meterUsage: Water used (100 cubic feet per unit)
checkMeter: Check readings and changes in use
previousUsage: Water used on the previous bill
rateNotCompared: We could not compare the rate. Check the dates, units and service details.
noMathIssue: No difference was found in this comparison.
billNotVerdict: A difference is a reason to ask for an explanation. It does not prove an overcharge. This check does not verify every line on your bill.
meterReset: The new reading is lower. Ask whether the meter was reset, replaced or rolled over.
meterMismatch: The meter readings do not match the water use entered. Recheck the numbers.
usageJump: Daily water use is over 50% higher than on the previous bill. Check for leaks, extra use or a billing change.

rateDifference: The water-use charge differs from this rate calculation.

advocacyHint: Get someone to respond, or speak up with neighbors.

yourQuestion: What do you need help with?
escalationIntro: Answer a few questions to find an appropriate office.
rentalHousing: A problem in a rented home
alreadyAsked: I already asked the responsible office for help
noResponse: I have not received a response
escalationNotLegal: Offices have different responsibilities. Confirm that an office handles your provider and issue. Deadlines can apply; a local legal-aid office can help.
routeProviderHelp: Ask for a written answer and a request number. Keep the date and a copy of what you sent.
routeDrinkingWaterHelp: This office oversees public drinking-water standards. Ask which office handles your water system or private well.
routeCommissionHelp: Some commissions handle privately owned utilities. City-owned services may be outside their authority.
routeMunicipalHelp: Ask the local government or utility about a billing review and the appeal process.
routeHousingHelp: Ask a local housing or legal-aid office about your landlord’s responsibilities and the local complaint process.
routeCivilRightsHelp: Describe the events and keep evidence. Different offices handle different types of discrimination. Do not assume one office covers every case.
routeLegalAidHelp: A local legal-aid office can explain your options and any deadlines. Availability and eligibility vary.
routeFollowupHelp: Include your original request date and receipt number. Ask for the next step and a response date.

statusOfficial: Check the office’s own status page.
statusHonesty: A case marked closed does not prove a repair is finished. Ask the office what was done. Your own notes are labeled separately from office records.
statusDelay: This public feed updates several times a day. It is not a live view of repair work.
caseNotFound: No matching case was found. Check the number and year, or use the office’s status page.
publicPromisesIntro: See recorded public commitments and their source links. These records are contributed by users.
noPromises: No public promises have been recorded for this place.
publicPromisePrivacy: Use only public statements and public source links. Do not include residents’ names, private addresses or personal records.
publishPromiseConsent: I reviewed this record and want these details to be public
promisePublished: Your record is public. Keep the private editing link below.
publicUnverified: User-contributed record. Check the original source.
publicUnavailable: Public sharing is not connected in this preview. You can prepare a record and keep it private.
whatYouAsked: What help did you ask for?
whyUnequal: Why do you believe you were treated differently? (optional)
treatmentPrivate: Record what happened in your own words. This does not decide whether discrimination occurred. Save supporting documents in your private records.
guideIntro: Short explanations to help you decide what to ask next.
guideText_lead: Lead can enter water from some pipes, fixtures and plumbing. A public report cannot confirm what comes from your own tap. Ask about your service line and a tap-water test. Boiling does not remove lead.
guideText_nitrate: Check whether the lab reports nitrate as nitrogen or as nitrate. Those numbers use different comparisons. Nitrate is especially important when water is used for infant formula. Ask the lab or health department what your result means.
guideText_arsenic: Keep the amount and units from your lab report. A filter must be certified for the relevant arsenic claim and water conditions. Do not assume every filter removes arsenic.
guideText_pfas: PFAS is a large group of chemicals. Match the exact names in your report to the filter’s verified claims. A claim for one chemical does not cover the whole group.
guideText_forms: Keep a copy of the original. Answer only what you know. Ask for an interpreter or accessible format if needed. Review every answer before signing or sending it. Keep the confirmation.
guideText_bills: Separate water use from sewer, fixed fees, old balances and credits. Compare the same units and billing dates. Ask the utility to explain a difference before calling it an overcharge.
toolIntro: Choose a task. You can use these tools without checking an address first.
pipeMapIntro: Use official maps where available. A neighborhood or water-system record does not prove what pipe serves your home.
mapExactOnly: Property details are shown only when an exact address record is available. Otherwise, ask for an inspection.
complaintFormsIntro: Choose an office, prepare the required details, then review and submit on its official route.
signatureNeeded: You must review and sign where required. This tool does not sign or submit for you.
complaintFacts: Describe what happened, when and where
complaintBasis: Why do you believe this was discrimination?
otherComplaints: Other complaints or court cases about this issue (optional)
filingPrivacy: Check the office’s privacy and public-records rules before sending personal details.
epaScope: EPA handles covered complaints against recipients of EPA funding. Review its filing rules and deadlines. Prepare your facts, then review, sign and send through the current official route.
pscScope: For a Florida utility regulated by the PSC. Confirm your company is listed on the official form. City-owned services and some other issues are outside its authority. The official form may make your information public.
